enonce_markdown:
Given that $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&5\end{pmatrix}$, find the matrix $AB$.

a) $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\19&22\end{pmatrix}$

b) $\begin{pmatrix}4&5\\11&20\end{pmatrix}$

c) $\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\6&20\end{pmatrix}$

d) $\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\5&9\end{pmatrix}$
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To multiply two $2\times2$ matrices, each entry of the product is the sum of the products of a row of the first matrix with a column of the second. The order matters: $AB\ne BA$ in general.

### Solution

$$AB=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&5\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2(1)+1(2)&2(0)+1(5)\\3(1)+4(2)&3(0)+4(5)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4&5\\11&20\end{pmatrix}$$

Option a is $BA$ (the order reversed); option c multiplies entry by entry; option d adds the matrices.

**Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown:
Find the determinant of the matrix $N=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$.

a) $-26$

b) $14$

c) $20$

d) $26$
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ the determinant is $ad-bc$. Take care with negative entries.

### Solution

$\det N=5(4)-(-2)(3)=20+6=26$.

Option b treats $(-2)(3)$ as $+6$ and subtracts it; option a is $bc-ad$; option c keeps only $ad$.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown:
Find the inverse of the matrix $M=\begin{pmatrix}4&3\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$.

a) $\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-2&4\end{pmatrix}$

b) $\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}4&-3\\-2&2\end{pmatrix}$

c) $\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-2&4\end{pmatrix}$

d) $\dfrac1{14}\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-2&4\end{pmatrix}$
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

For $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ with $ad-bc\ne0$, the inverse is $\dfrac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}$: swap the diagonal entries, change the signs of the other two, divide by the determinant.

### Solution

$\det M=4(2)-3(2)=2$, so

$$M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-2&4\end{pmatrix}.$$

Check: $M M^{-1}=\dfrac12\begin{pmatrix}8-6&-12+12\\4-4&-6+8\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

Option b does not swap the diagonal entries; option c forgets the factor $\dfrac1{\det M}$; option d uses $4(2)+3(2)=14$ as the determinant.

**Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown:
Use matrices to solve the simultaneous equations
$$3x+y=7,\qquad 5x+2y=11.$$
*[5 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Write the system as $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$, then multiply both sides on the left by the inverse matrix: $\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=A^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}$.

### Solution

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\5&2\end{pmatrix}$, so $A\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}7\\11\end{pmatrix}$.

$\det A=3(2)-1(5)=1$, so $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-5&3\end{pmatrix}$.

$$\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-5&3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}7\\11\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}14-11\\-35+33\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}.$$

Check: $3(3)+(-2)=7$ and $5(3)+2(-2)=11$.

**$x=3$, $y=-2$.**

enonce_markdown:
The matrix $P=\begin{pmatrix}k&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ has no inverse. Find the value of $k$.

a) $-\dfrac32$

b) $\dfrac23$

c) $\dfrac32$

d) $6$
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A $2\times2$ matrix has no inverse exactly when its determinant $ad-bc$ is zero (the matrix is singular).

### Solution

$\det P=4k-2(3)=4k-6$. Set $4k-6=0$, so $k=\dfrac64=\dfrac32$.

Check: with $k=\dfrac32$, the first row $\left(\dfrac32,2\right)$ is $\dfrac12$ of the second row $(3,4)$, so the matrix is singular.

Option d forgets to divide by $4$; option b inverts the fraction; option a has a sign error.

**Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: Given that $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&5\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\7&2\end{pmatrix}$, find the matrix $X$ such that $AX=B$. *[6 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

If $AX=B$ and $A$ has an inverse, multiply both sides on the LEFT by $A^{-1}$: $X=A^{-1}B$. The order matters, because matrix multiplication is not commutative.

### Solution

$\det A=1(5)-2(3)=-1$, so $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-5&2\\3&-1\end{pmatrix}$.

$$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{pmatrix}-5&2\\3&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\7&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-20+14&-5+4\\12-7&3-2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-6&-1\\5&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Check: $AX=\begin{pmatrix}-6+10&-1+2\\-18+25&-3+5\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\7&2\end{pmatrix}=B$.

**$X=\begin{pmatrix}-6&-1\\5&1\end{pmatrix}$.**
